**Observations:**
- Affected part: fruit (bell peppers)
- Large, dark brown-to-black, sunken circular lesions on both fruits
- Concentric ring pattern visible within the lesions
- Lesion texture is collapsed/wrinkled with a darker border
- No fuzzy mycelium, no stem involvement

**Reasoning:**
The concentric-ringed, sunken, dark lesions on pepper fruit are the textbook presentation of **Anthracnose** (caused by *Colletotrichum* spp.). The acervuli-dotted concentric rings, dark coloration, and sunken necrotic tissue are all hallmarks. Gray Mold would show fuzzy gray sporulation; Rhizopus Soft Rot would be mushy with coarse black sporangia; Alternaria would favor leaves/stems with a different ring pattern. Nothing in the image points elsewhere.
